name: Estimation Station
description: Practice estimating large quantities. You write a few 'how many...?' challenges (jelly beans in a jar, breaths in a day, grains of rice in a cup), students each guess a number on their device, and the class sees how close everyone got, plus the class's average guess, which is often closer than almost anyone's. Great for number sense, Fermi problems, and 'guess the quantity' warm-ups.
tagline: How many jelly beans are in the jar? Let the whole class find out.

questions.label: Estimation challenges
questions.helper: One round per challenge. Give the real number and what it's counting, students guess, then the class sees who came closest.

prompt.label: The challenge
prompt.placeholder: How many jelly beans are in this jar?

default.prompt: How many jelly beans would fill a 1-gallon jar?
How many times does an average person's heart beat in a single day?
How many grains of rice are in a single cup?

scoring.label: How points work
scoring.helper: graduated: everyone earns points, more for being closer (kinder, keeps the whole class in it). closest: the single closest guess takes all the points.

questionTimer.label: Seconds per challenge
questionTimer.helper: Estimating well takes a little thinking, 45 seconds is a good default.

template.name: Estimation Station
template.description: Guess the quantity, closest guesses earn the most, and the class average is the one to beat.

intro.message:
ESTIMATION STATION!

Each round you'll see a 'how many...?' challenge. Type your best estimate, no need to be exact, just reason it out.

Closest guesses earn the most points. And watch the class's average guess: a whole room together is usually closer than almost anyone alone.

end.message: Nice estimating, everyone! The more you practice, the sharper your number sense gets.
